newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds' bullish year limps to an end.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds' bullish year limps to an end.

text.p: *The Australian bond market's generally bullish year ended in a bit of an anti-climax with futures prices marginally softer on the day and the turnover seasonally light.
The Australian bond market's generally bullish year ended in a bit of an anti-climax with futures prices marginally softer on the day and the turnover seasonally light.
Futures trading through the screen-based SYCOM system ended at 12.30 p.m. (0130 GMT) and resumes as normal at 8.30 a.m. (2130 GMT) on Thursday. There is no afterhours trading in the interim period.
The softer bias reflected a fairly inactive U.S. Treasury market in New York, which gave up the gains seen in overseas trading on Monday, and due to the holiday in Japan today.
Traders doubt that activity will get back into full swing until next week when the domestic data flow resumes, starting with the November balance of payments on Monday.

The ten-year bond futures contract ended the year at 92.520 down from Monday's 92.540 close and some 50 basis points below the near-three year high of 93.015 seen in early December. The front position futures contract ended last year at 91.760.

The debt market faces one last event of the year with the result of an A$800 million Treasury note tender at 2.00 p.m. (0300 GMT) which sees A$200 million of five-week, A$200 million of 13-week and A$400 million of 26-week maturities on offer.

Local bond yield spreads ended with a tighter bias, although the long-end of the Canadian debt market outshone the dollar bloc. The Australian/U.S. 10-year margin scraped below resistance at 110 basis points, although no dramatic moves are expected until the market gets a fresh slug of local data.
